This podcast is for informational purposes. only and should not be relied upon as a basis for investment decisions. In this episode, I speak with Martin Tarley, a portfolio manager at GMO spearheading their work on Nibo, a goals-based investment platform.

key_points.text: Martin described Nibo as, quote, bridging the gap between financial planning and portfolio management, end quote.
key_points.evidence_quote: Martin described Nibo as, quote, bridging the gap between financial planning and portfolio management, end quote, with the key innovation being the reformulation of risk from volatility to not having what you need slash want when you need slash want it.

key_points.text: In other words, constraints on both wealth target and horizon.
key_points.evidence_quote: In other words, constraints on both wealth target and horizon.

key_points.text: This reformulation of the core problem introduces a number of complications to the portfolio optimization process.
key_points.evidence_quote: This reformulation of the core problem introduces a number of complications to the portfolio optimization process.

key_points.text: For example, under classic power utility, lower volatility is always preferred.
key_points.evidence_quote: For example, under classic power utility, lower volatility is always preferred.

thesis: The episode discusses the significant gap between financial planning and asset management that financial advisors struggle with, noting that the industry has historically focused too much on the investment problem rather than the investor problem. The speakers argue that the core issue involves balancing short-term considerations with long-term objectives and reformulating risk from volatility to the constraint of not having what you need or want when you need or want it.
